Love this game and played a lot of the demo, but it needs a huge balancing overhaul. Keeping crowns in the earlier levels is near impossible, while your later-round builds are made almost irrelevant by the introduction of late-game towers like the Tower of Defense. The game has a lot of potential but I think the numbers need to be looked at--the challenge is impossible sometimes. Not difficult, straight-up impossible. That paired with your limited options for choosing and removing towers makes too many runs feel RNG-based. Can't recommend as is, but I'll reevaluate this review after an update or two.

When I first started playing the demon faction I thought it was overpowered, but I haven't been able to beat the first boss once in probably 20 tries. The mechanics aren't leveling up enough or there isn't enough mana to go around because I almost never have a winning board unless I get extremely lucky with a Glutton demon, rations tower, the fryer and cookpot combo, and succubus consuming glitch. Needs a bit more oomph in the numbers here because it's just not coming together.

This game has an excellent concept which the execute on just about as poorly as they could. The main issue is the balancing. The first boss is one of those kinds of bosses where you have to have a specific kind of build to be able to beat it. Which basically means 70% of the strategies you might want to play around with are invalid and worthless. So many towers are very interesting and I'd like to try to make work, but with the first boss checking you SO hard there's not time to try and make those longer term builds work, ans you can really only use a handful of highly aggressive builds to play. What's worse is with how rng based the tower selection js, you'll more than likely lose on the first boss to a majority of these runs. Not because you messed up, or because you didn't have the skills, but simply because it was mathematically impossible for you to win with the tower section you got. This is the worst aspect of this game, it's down to pure numbers on if you get past the first boss, and those numbers are in rngs hand more than yours.

tl.dr. fun game idea, but balancing makes most strategies and many towers impossible to play, often leading to reliance on pure rng in the early. This also leads to middle and late game being boring as viable strategies scale too good (Bear, Obisidian, Flower, Honey). Interactivity is minimal during middle to late game, either strategies run by themselve or the strategy has already failed. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ I love the idea and I think the game can be great fun, but the balancing is bad. The enemies scale exponentially, but most available winning conditions scale linear, so they just can't keep up (f.ex. Cat, Frog). Those that can keep up (Obsidian, Flower and Bear) are so strong, that they barely pose any challenge after the first boss. Also infernal is a cool game mode, but the winning conditions are even worse. Mole is so badly hindered by its debuff on lvl 1 (has to tank one attack before it can retaliate), that then first boss is almost impossible without getting him lvl2 (3! 5 cost hits), the vampire and blood tower strategy is also incapale of surviving the first boss etc. I would also like to add the lack for margin of error. Wrongly places turrets can immeadiatly ruin a run, resources to reposition or remove are scarce (although there are far more than the demo had), which makes the first rounds frustratring to play. Commiting to the wrong strategy, sometimes necessary to not die within the first rounds, can deny future winouts, as necessary space is blocked by useless towers. This is not as critical as my previous point, but is takes away flexibility and normalizes restarting the game to prevent a bad start. Interactivity during later rounds is also limited. There is little point in leaving spaces open, from then on it is mostly rerolling and scaling up towers. Rearranging, deleting is rarely usefull in the middle to late game (which is usually when the options become available) as the boards, that would requier those tokens have already failed. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Edit: I have continued to play the game and my opinion has hardened on the bad balancing. Especially Inferno suffers from poor balancing choices that make all theoretically plausible strategies pure luck based on whether you hit all(!) towers in time and don't make any mistakes in placement or tower choice. Plus, why are so many strategies nerfed right from the get go? Like, why does Drover kill anything below 10 HP? It makes it impossible to combine it with many other towers, as those need to have their HP increased significantly. (f.e. succubus needs 8 HP point, which is 8 rounds of sacrifize without blood tower, ~16 points of mana) Yes, it makes sense with goblin, but why not reduce goblin hp significantly over all levels, so this issue doens't arise and Drover can actually be used in a strategy without skipping him for the first 5 rounds?

I actually think this makes the balance correct - what's the point in playing a game where you can brainlessly pick whatever you'd like? I'm not going to spoil anything, but all I'll say is that if you enjoyed the demo, the EA release game only builds on that. I've personally been enjoying it very much.

The game is very anti-fun because of how poorly balanced it is. As you can see from the reviews, it has a fun base, but many are noting how poor the balance is and the dev does not seem that interested in fixing it. The issue is most builds are too reliant on rng to get going + early game scales too fast. You will find your first main tower level up will often be a straight stat increase just to survive and you will be praying that you get the uncommon or rare towers you need fast enough to not just lose. And because you need your builds online asap to make it passed the mid game, you cannot use filler towers to help you survive the early game as that delays your build coming online. So you lose to rng, not skill. With many builds needing a literal perfect early game to even beat the first boss or get passed the mid game. By perfect, I mean perfect. Many builds also do not scale well at all. Some towers get +1 per tower level, others double. And many are meant to be weak at first then scale...but the scaling is linear when the enemies are growing exponentially. So you barely beat the third act and only a few builds can get anywhere in endless. Many builds that work in the demo fall off in the full game for that reason (ex: butler). The first boss in particular is a brutal dps check. It invalidates a ton of builds as it only cares about you doing 100 damage (or more with ascensions) to it. And the third boss is harder then the final boss really. Ascension makes the problems worse. What makes this worse is some builds are balanced properly (ex: cat and prism). But, then the rest just does not follow what makes builds work at all. Some are so bad that you should never even bother to use the tower. Which is why I think the game is anti-fun. It shows you all these possible fun builds, but then you feel stupid for not doing anything but the one good build that works for the tower pack.

The game is addictive. You want to keep going, again and again and again. Yet you die. There are nearly no viable builds here. The game scales fast, and you must out-scale this exponentially BEFORE round 10 or else you will not even make it past the first boss. In truth, you will know by round 4 if you will be able to scale beyond level 10 or get absolutely rekt. And so you lose, you try again, the game wipes the floor with your sorry, addicted krack-head *ss. And you come back... And sometimes, once every 100 tries, you will find a build which takes you to the heights of victory you could not even imagine in your wildest dreams. And it gives you hope, so you keep playing, and the game breaks you again, and again and again. So I made it a mission to beat it, to beat it so hard I could feel its miserable life slip between my fingers. Finally I did it. Played the game beyond its boundaries. With the pirate tower, took it to level 50 at least... But I will never know how far I could have gone, because the game CRASHED (screenshot available on demand)! Even in victory, it will find a way to take your happiness away from you. Yet I smile a little, because I did it. I broke it, just this one time. My vengence, as bittersweet as it is, brings me a cold joy - one that I will never fully cherish. This must be what an abusive relationship is. Do not get involved
